reproduction_target: Statistical-method paper (weighted t-test / chi-square DGE for scRNASeq and spRNASeq without distributional model assumptions) with an accompanying wet-lab-generated spatial dataset. Computational reproduction target: SpaceRanger processing of the newly generated Visium HD mouse-tibia run; Loupe Browser image substitution and proliferating-chondrocyte area/barcode export; Seurat import + merge + marker-gene-based neuron selection from two public 10X E18 mouse-brain scRNASeq datasets; in-silico noise / up-regulation and count-subsampling simulations; the authors' custom weighted-t-test/chi-square DGE functions; comparator runs of Seurat FindMarkers (Wilcoxon, t-test), SCTransform v2 and DESeq2 pseudo-bulk; figure plotting. Mouse husbandry, tibia dissection/fixation/sectioning/H&E staining, microscopy and the Visium HD bench assay itself are wet-lab and out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis from STAR METHODS 'METHOD DETAILS' + 'QUANTIFICATION AND STATISTICAL ANALYSIS' prose, plus the code/data availability statements. Stage-1 prose read only: the repository landing page and README prose were read, but no R source file was opened (that is Stage 2). The repo (https://github.com/sergeyleikin/sc-sp-RNASeq) contains CodeForScSpRNASeqPaper_v4.R described in the README as 'R code used to generate results in the main text of the paper (Figs. 1-6)' together with the two preassembled .rds inputs, so the code axis is credited as reconstructable-to-likely-exact at prose level, but the paper cites only the bare repo URL with no commit SHA, tag, or archival DOI, so no exact-artifact pin is claimed. Wet-lab steps counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: Visium HD sequencing-data processing with SpaceRanger v.3.0.1 (10X Genomics); CytAssist low-resolution image replaced by high-resolution Nikon Ti2-E image 'as described by the manufacturer'
Loupe Browser (10X Genomics) manual selection of proliferating-chondrocyte areas in 3 tibia growth plates and export of 8x8 um bin barcodes for downstream R analysis

Import of two public 10X E18 mouse-brain scRNASeq filtered feature .h5 matrices into Seurat objects, merge without renormalization, and marker-based cell selection (GABAergic: nonzero Gad1/Gad2/Slc6a1; glutamatergic: nonzero Gls/Grin2b/Slc17a7)

In-silico simulation of random noise f_n(alpha, N) and expression up/down-regulation f_ex on the glutamatergic-neuron count matrix (alpha = 5 selected mid-range; beta = 1.5 for 50% upregulation), plus 40% UMI count subsampling

Authors' custom weighted-average / weighted t-test and chi-square DGE analysis (Seurat-compatible R functions sc&spRNASeqFunctions_v2*.R; two-tailed, unequal variances), including per-gene QC minima and FDR adjustment
Comparator DGE with Seurat v.5.2.0 FindMarkers (default Wilcoxon; optional t-test on log-normalized data; t-test on relative-count normalized data) and SCTransform version 2 with default parameters
Pseudo-bulk comparator: random cell subsetting into two 5-sample sets, count aggregation, and DESeq2 testing (Seurat's default PB route)
Figure/plot generation with SigmaPlot v.13.0 (Systat Software) for all published plots

Mouse husbandry and tissue collection: C57BL/6J (JAX #000664) E18.5 embryo tibia dissection, 4% formaldehyde fixation 24 h, paraffin embedding, sectioning, H&E staining, Nikon Ti2-E 20X/0.8NA imaging (ACUC-approved protocol)
Visium HD (10X Genomics) spatial assay incl. CytAssist capture and sequencing (356,837,522 reads; 1080 mean reads per 8x8 um bin; 89.3% valid barcodes; 99.9% valid UMIs; 28.5% saturation)

headline.static_readiness: 0/8 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 5/8 computational steps (63%) reach RI, the stage-1 ceiling: data are public (GEO GSE299816, Synapse syn66520062, two named 10X public scRNASeq datasets), the analysis code that generated main-text Figs. 1-6 is public in a live GitHub repo, and R 4.4.2 / RStudio 2024.12.0 build 467 / Seurat 5.2.0 / SpaceRanger 3.0.1 are exactly pinned in prose. Version stays capped at 1 because there is no environment closure (no renv.lock, no conda env, no container, no sessionInfo) - the pins are prose-level only. Three steps cap at NI: Loupe Browser manual area selection (GUI, unversioned, no code artifact), the DESeq2 pseudo-bulk comparator (DESeq2 version never stated), and SigmaPlot v13.0 plotting (proprietary GUI, no script). Under the strictest reading the repo reference is a floating main-branch URL with no commit SHA, tag, or archival DOI cited in the paper, and the README documents that the analysis functions have already drifted (v2b -> v2i -> v2j, with v2j behaving differently from v2i), so the code axis could reasonably be argued down.
headline.coverage: 8 computational steps assessed from STAR-METHODS prose and the code/data availability statements; 2 wet-lab steps counted (W) and verdicted X as out of computational-reproduction scope. Repo landing page and README prose were read; no R source file was opened at this stage.

gaps.where: Software environment for all R-based steps (C3-C7) and the vendor pipeline (C1)
gaps.missing: No environment closure of any kind. Exact prose pins exist (R v.4.4.2, RStudio v.2024.12.0 build 467, Seurat v.5.2.0, SpaceRanger v.3.0.1, SigmaPlot v.13.0) but there is no renv.lock, no conda/pixi lockfile, no Docker/Singularity image or digest, no sessionInfo() dump, and no requirements list. Transitive R dependencies (Matrix, MatrixExtra, DESeq2, sctransform) are unpinned.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship an renv.lock (or a container digest) captured from the machine that produced the figures, and include sessionInfo() output alongside CodeForScSpRNASeqPaper_v4.R.

gaps.where: Code-availability statement and every repo citation in the paper
gaps.missing: The paper cites only the bare, mutable repository URL https://github.com/sergeyleikin/sc-sp-RNASeq with no commit SHA, no tag, and no archival DOI (Zenodo / Software Heritage). The repo has in fact been modified after the preprint (README documents updates on 3/13/2026, 3/17/2026 and 5/27/2026; the DGE function file moved v2b -> v2i -> v2j with an explicitly stated behavioural/performance change), so the URL no longer resolves to the state used for the reported results.
gaps.how_to_close: Cite an immutable reference: mint a Zenodo DOI for the paper-state snapshot, or at minimum cite the commit SHA / release tag corresponding to the version used for Figs. 1-6.

gaps.where: C2 Loupe Browser region selection; C8 SigmaPlot plotting
gaps.missing: Two steps in the published figure path are interactive proprietary GUI operations with no scriptable artifact. The proliferating-chondrocyte area selection determines which 8x8 um bins enter the spatial DGE analysis and was done by hand in Loupe Browser (version not stated); all published plots were drawn in SigmaPlot v13.0 with no exported script or settings.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exported barcode lists per selected area (the repo does ship a preassembled E18tib.PCN.rds, which partially covers this) and state the Loupe Browser version; regenerate plots from a scripted plotting routine, or deposit the plot input tables.

gaps.missing: DESeq2 version is never stated anywhere in the paper, and neither is the Seurat AggregateExpression / pseudo-bulk configuration (test type, fitType, independent filtering, shrinkage). Given the paper's central claim is that this comparator produces the most false findings, its exact configuration is load-bearing.
gaps.how_to_close: State the DESeq2 version and full call parameters for the pseudo-bulk comparison, and confirm whether Seurat defaults or DESeq2 defaults were used.

gaps.where: C4 simulations and C7 random cell subsetting
gaps.missing: All simulations are stochastic (uniform random noise draws, random count subsampling to 40%, random cell subsetting into two 5-sample sets, 10 repeated simulations) and no random seed or seeding strategy is stated in the Methods prose.
gaps.how_to_close: State the RNG seed(s) and R RNGkind in the Methods, or set them explicitly in the deposited script.

gaps.where: C1 SpaceRanger invocation and CytAssist image substitution
gaps.missing: SpaceRanger v3.0.1 is pinned but no command line, reference transcriptome build/version, probe-set version, or binning parameters are given; the high-resolution image substitution is described only as 'as described by the manufacturer'.
gaps.how_to_close: Provide the spaceranger count command, the reference transcriptome and probe-set identifiers with versions, and the exact image-alignment procedure/files.

gaps.missing: The public GEO record GSE299816 covers the spatial data, but the manually selected proliferating-chondrocyte bin sets used for Fig. 6 are only available via a preassembled .rds convenience object in the repo; the selection provenance (which bins, by what criteria beyond the stated QC thresholds) is not machine-readable independently of that object.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the per-area barcode lists as plain text alongside the .rds, with the QC filter applied as code.

gaps.where: W1-W2: mouse husbandry, tibia dissection/fixation/paraffin embedding/sectioning/H&E, microscopy, Visium HD bench assay and sequencing
gaps.missing: Wet-lab data-generation steps are out of scope for Tier-1 computational reproduction; counted in W and verdicted X.
